summary: The week of June 8–14 closed with 32.0 km across 4 runs, anchored by a strong 17.6 km long run at 6:17/km with 106m elevation on Sunday. The current week (June 15–21) is just starting — no runs logged on Monday or Tuesday yet — placing you in a brief recovery window before Wednesday's scheduled VO2max session. With the Porto Half Marathon 89 days out and the Marathon 145 days out, you are in the early base-building phase where aerobic volume and weekly long run progression are the top priorities.
key_observations: The 17.6 km long run on June 14 at 6:17/km is the strongest aerobic stimulus of the last 14 days — 106m of elevation adds good neuromuscular load; extending this to 19–21 km over the next 3–4 Sundays is the single most important step toward half marathon readiness.

The 5.0 km at 4:48/km on June 11 shows solid speed, but replacing ad-hoc fast efforts with Wednesday's structured VO2max intervals (4×4 min at max effort with 3 min walking recovery) will produce more reliable aerobic ceiling gains.

Outside the long run, weekly easy volume (6.0 km + 3.4 km) is on the low side for marathon base — adding one extra easy run of 8–10 km on a currently empty day would raise weekly aerobic stimulus without meaningful fatigue.
focus_next_week: Execute Wednesday's VO2max interval session at true max effort while fully rested, then prioritise Sunday's long run — target 19 km at easy pace (6:30–7:00/km) to maintain progressive overload after last Sunday's 17.6 km.
